# Knowledge Base: erdos-211-incomplete-01

## Evidence Snapshot

Local gallery metadata for `erdos-211` reports `sorries: 0`, `axiomCount: 10`, `theoremCount: 1`, `definitionCount: 9`, and badge `axiom`. The Lean source in this worktree is `proofs/Proofs/Erdos211Problem.lean`; the metadata path omits the top-level `proofs/` prefix.

## Problem Understanding

Erdos Problem #211 is the solved incidence-geometry result: if n planar points have at most n-k points on any line, with 1 <= k < n, then they determine Omega(k n) lines containing at least two points. The Lean theorem `erdos_211` states this result, but its proof is `beck_szemeredi_trotter n k P hn hk hcol`, where `beck_szemeredi_trotter` is an axiom.

## Current Formalization Surface

The file defines the basic geometry/counting vocabulary (`Point`, `Line`, `Collinear`, `numLines`, `maxCollinear`, `HasBoundedCollinearity`, `formedLines`, `incidences`) and states several major incidence results as axioms. The 10 axioms are `beck_szemeredi_trotter`, `special_case_quadratic`, `beck_dichotomy`, `beck_quantitative`, `szemeredi_trotter`, `rich_lines_bound`, `constant_one_sixth_optimal`, `bgs_configuration`, `furedi_palasti_optimal`, and `crossing_number_inequality`.

## Conservative Status

This record should not be marked complete. There are no sorries to fill, but the parent theorem depends on unproved axioms. The immediate research value is an axiom audit and possible reduction of the assumption surface.
